why: rclcpp_action's `ServerGoalHandle::execute()`, moved off the handle onto `(server, goal)`. our goal handle is a 16-byte UUID TOKEN, not an owning object: `rclc_goal_handle_t` holds the uuid and nothing else, and every lifecycle fact lives in the executor's static goal arena (read back with `rclc_action_get_goal_status`). rcl's `rcl_action_goal_handle_t` is allocator-constructed, carries its own state machine and is finalised by the caller -- no allocator, so there is nothing to construct, nothing to fini, and no object to hang the lifecycle methods on. It is also why our terminal verbs take `(server, goal)` where rclcpp's are members: see `c:action_succeed`.
